stories.headline: Anthropic releases Opus 4.8, its most advanced model, tuned to flag its own uncertainty

key_facts.fact: Anthropic released Opus 4.8 on Thursday, May 28, calling it the newest version of its most advanced publicly available model, available everywhere at the same standard pricing as Opus 4.7.
key_facts.excerpt: On Thursday, Anthropic released Opus 4.8, the newest version of its most advanced publicly available model. The model is available everywhere, with standard pricing at the same level as the previous Opus release.

key_facts.fact: The model arrived just 41 days after Opus 4.7, a much faster upgrade cycle than normal for Anthropic, amid pressure from new OpenAI Codex and Google Gemini Flash releases.
key_facts.excerpt: The new model comes just 41 days after Opus 4.7 was released, a much faster upgrade cycle than normal for Anthropic.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic's early testers found the new model is 'more likely to flag uncertainties about its work and less likely to make unsupported claims.'
key_facts.excerpt: In the launch post, Anthropic's early testers found that the new model is 'more likely to flag uncertainties about its work and less likely to make unsupported claims.'

key_facts.fact: A Bridgewater testimonial said the biggest difference was Opus 4.8's tendency to proactively flag issues with the inputs and outputs of an analysis that other models routinely missed.
key_facts.excerpt: a testimonial from Bridgewater associates said the biggest difference in the upgrade was 'Opus 4.8's tendency to proactively flag issues with the inputs and outputs of an analysis, something other models routinely missed.'

key_facts.fact: Anthropic said it is still holding back its most advanced Mythos model over cybersecurity concerns but expects to bring Mythos-class models to all customers 'in the coming weeks.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'We're making swift progress on developing these safeguards and expect to be able to bring Mythos-class models to all our customers in the coming weeks,' the company wrote.

stories.headline: Anthropic raises $65B at $965B valuation, overtaking OpenAI as most valuable AI startup

key_facts.fact: Anthropic announced a $65 billion Series H financing at a $965 billion post-money valuation on Thursday, May 28.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic has snagged $65 billion in funding at a $965 billion post-money valuation in its latest funding round, marking what could be the AI startup's last private fundraising before debuting on the public markets.

key_facts.fact: The valuation pushes Anthropic above OpenAI, which was valued at $852 billion in late March after a record $122 billion round.
key_facts.excerpt: The financing puts its value above rival AI lab OpenAI. OpenAI was valued at $852 billion in late March after closing a record-breaking $122 billion funding round.

key_facts.fact: The round was led by Altimeter Capital, Dragoneer, Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital, and nearly triples Anthropic's $380 billion valuation from February.
key_facts.excerpt: The newest round was led by Altimeter Capital, Dragoneer, Greenoaks, and Sequoia Capital and almost triples its valuation from February, when it was worth $380 billion.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic reported a $47 billion revenue run rate, up from a $30 billion run rate earlier this year and $10 billion in revenue last year, driven by its Claude Code coding assistant.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic also reported a $47 billion revenue run rate on Thursday. That's up from $30 billion run rate earlier this year, and $10 billion in revenue last year.

key_facts.fact: The round includes $15 billion of previously committed hyperscaler investments, including $5 billion from Amazon, with infrastructure partners such as Micron also contributing.
key_facts.excerpt: The round includes $15 billion of previously committed hyperscaler investments, including $5 billion from Amazon. Infrastructure partners, including Micron Technology... also contributed.

stories.headline: Anthropic adds dynamic workflows to Claude Code, fanning out hundreds of parallel subagents

key_facts.fact: Anthropic introduced dynamic workflows in Claude Code on May 28, where Claude writes orchestration scripts that run tens to hundreds of parallel subagents in a single session and checks its work before returning results.
key_facts.excerpt: Claude dynamically writes orchestration scripts that run tens to hundreds of parallel subagents in a single session, checking its work before anything reaches you.

key_facts.fact: Dynamic workflows launched in research preview across the Claude Code CLI, Desktop and VS Code extension for Max, Team and Enterprise plans, and on the Claude API, Amazon Bedrock, Vertex AI and Microsoft Foundry.
key_facts.excerpt: Dynamic workflows are available today in research preview in the Claude Code CLI, Desktop, and the VS code extension for Max, Team, and Enterprise... as well as on the Claude API, on Amazon Bedrock, Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic cited the rewrite of Bun: Jarred Sumner used dynamic workflows to port Bun from Zig to Rust with 99.8% of the existing test suite passing, roughly 750,000 lines of Rust, in eleven days from first commit to merge.
key_facts.excerpt: Jarred Sumner used dynamic workflows to port Bun from Zig to Rust with 99.8% of the existing test suite passing, roughly 750,000 lines of Rust, and eleven days from first commit to merge.

key_facts.fact: The company said Claude Code with Opus 4.8 can now carry out codebase-scale migrations across hundreds of thousands of lines of code from kickoff to merge, using the existing test suite as its bar.
key_facts.excerpt: 'Claude Code alongside Opus 4.8 can now carry out codebase-scale migrations across hundreds of thousands of lines of code from kickoff to merge, with the existing test suite as its bar,' the post explains.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic warned that dynamic workflows can consume substantially more tokens than a typical Claude Code session and recommended starting on a scoped task.
key_facts.excerpt: Dynamic workflows can consume substantially more tokens than a typical Claude Code session, so we recommend starting on a scoped task to get a feel for usage in your work.

stories.headline: OpenAI launches Rosalind Biodefense Program, offering its GPT-Rosalind model to trusted developers

key_facts.fact: OpenAI announced its Rosalind Biodefense Program, which will offer its GPT-Rosalind model for life sciences research to 'trusted developers' building biodefense tools.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI's new Rosalind Biodefense Program will offer its GPT-Rosalind model for life sciences research to 'trusted developers' operationalizing biodefense tools.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI said it will sponsor access and provide launch support for epidemiological modeling, early detection, screening, preparedness, non-pharmaceutical interventions and other public-health work.
key_facts.excerpt: The company will sponsor access to the tool and provide launch support for epidemiological modeling, early detection, screening, preparedness, non-pharmaceutical interventions and other public-health work.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI said it briefed the White House and several federal agencies on its approach and is expanding access to GPT-Rosalind for select U.S. government and allied partners.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI said it briefed the White House and several federal agencies on its approach... The company is also expanding access to GPT-Rosalind for select U.S. government and allied partners to support public health and biodefense missions.

key_facts.fact: The program is part of a broader OpenAI biodefense push that includes backing startups, convening government officials, and a Preparedness Framework that enforces stricter safeguards as model biological capabilities rise.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI is making a serious push into biodefense, backing startups, convening government officials, and developing AI tools designed to detect and mitigate biological threats... OpenAI also maintains what it calls a Preparedness Framework.

stories.headline: Reactor exits stealth with $59M to build a platform for real-time generative video

key_facts.fact: Reactor emerged from stealth on May 28 with $59 million in funding led by Lightspeed Venture Partners, with participation from WndrCo, Amplify Partners, Sky9 Capital, FPV Ventures and others.
key_facts.excerpt: Reactor, the developer platform for real-time generative video, today emerged from stealth with $59 million in funding led by Lightspeed Venture Partners, with participation from WndrCo, Amplify Partners, Sky9 Capital, FPV Ventures, and additional investors.

key_facts.fact: Reactor describes itself as the developer platform for real-time generative video, aiming to make real-time world models accessible to developers, and is headquartered in San Francisco.
key_facts.excerpt: Reactor is the developer platform for real-time generative video. Its mission is to make real-time world models accessible to developers everywhere... headquartered in San Francisco, California.

key_facts.fact: The $59 million spans seed and Series A funding, with backers including former DreamWorks chief Jeffrey Katzenberg.
key_facts.excerpt: Reactor, which says its AI platform can generate video in real-time with near-zero latency, emerges from stealth with a $59M Series A led by Lightspeed.

stories.headline: Apollo and Blackstone shop a $36B debt deal to buy Google TPUs for Anthropic to lease

key_facts.fact: Apollo Global Management and Blackstone are working to bring additional investors into a roughly $36 billion debt financing deal to help Anthropic build out its AI infrastructure.
key_facts.excerpt: Apollo Global Management Inc. and Blackstone Inc. are working to bring additional investors into a roughly $36 billion debt financing deal to help Anthropic PBC build out its AI infrastructure.

key_facts.fact: The debt does not sit on Anthropic's balance sheet; it flows through a special-purpose vehicle that buys Google's custom TPUs and leases the hardware back to Anthropic for data centres in New York, Texas, Louisiana and Indiana.
key_facts.excerpt: The borrowed money flows through a special-purpose vehicle that buys Google's custom tensor processing units... and then leases that hardware to Anthropic for use in data centres in New York, Texas, Louisiana and Indiana.

key_facts.fact: Broadcom, which helps Google build the TPUs, is providing a residual-value support agreement on roughly $31 billion of the senior debt, effectively underwriting demand for its own chips if Anthropic stops paying and resale value falls short.
key_facts.excerpt: Broadcom, which helps Google build the TPUs, is providing a residual-value support agreement on roughly $31 billion of the senior debt... if Anthropic stops paying its lease and the used chips do not fetch enough on resale to cover the loan, Broadcom absorbs the shortfall.

key_facts.fact: Investors were asked to submit orders this week with the deal expected to close the following week, in what could become one of the largest private credit deals in history and the biggest chip financing debt deal to date.
key_facts.excerpt: This transaction is set to become one of the largest private credit deals in history and the biggest chip financing debt deal to date... Investors have been asked to submit their subscription intentions soon, with the deal expected to close the following week.

key_facts.fact: The TPUs serve as Anthropic's alternative to a Nvidia-only chip supply, and Apollo and Blackstone plan to sell down part of the debt while retaining significant portions themselves.
key_facts.excerpt: Apollo and Blackstone also plan to sell down part of the debt after arranging it while keeping meaningful stakes, a setup that lets them recycle balance sheets and potentially repeat the structure for future AI buildouts.
